tool: Built-in image_gen; original source atlases, no Minecraft PNG copies
metal-atlas.png: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production Minecraft-style 16x16 pixel art texture atlas for a voxel mod. Create a perfectly regular square 4 by 4 sprite sheet, exactly 16 cells, each cell its own logical 16 by 16 pixel grid, nearest-neighbor crisp pixels. NO labels, no grid lines, no padding between cells. Entire sheet uses neutral grayscale only, 6 discrete flat gray shades, no hue. Rows 1, 2, 4 have transparent backgrounds. Row 3 is fully filled seamless block tiles. Row 1: four distinct refined metal ingot inventory sprites, classic compact Minecraft ingot shape, bevels, bright upper-left pixel highlights, dark lower/right edge, subtly different flat top shapes and bands; no gems or magic glow. Row 2: four rough raw alloy sample clusters, angular ore chunks with visible mottled metal patches, each compact 12x11 pixel silhouette, no debris. Row 3: four full 16x16 storage block faces, vanilla modern Minecraft metal texture style, respectively broad subtly hammered panels, riveted metal plate, lightly banded cast metal, small rectangular interlocking plates. Not high contrast black stripes. Row 4: four item sprites: a netherite-shaped pickaxe, a sword, helmet, boots with ordinary brown/dark handles where appropriate; all in neutral grayscale. Maintain vanilla Minecraft pixel density, simple readable silhouettes and selective highlights, no gradients, no anti aliasing, no 3D rendering, no smooth illustration, no tiny fake pixels, no text. This will be exported at precisely 64x64 logical pixels; keep shapes aligned to that grid.
equipment-atlas.png: Use case: stylized-concept. Production game texture asset: one regular 4-column, 2-row inventory equipment atlas, wide 2:1 aspect ratio, transparent background. Exactly eight equal square cells, no borders, no text, no shadows outside objects. Every cell is a logical 16 by 16 pixel Minecraft inventory sprite, enlarged using nearest-neighbor only. Row 1 left to right: pickaxe, sword, axe, shovel. Row 2 left to right: hoe, helmet, chestplate, pair of boots. Vanilla modern Minecraft style and recognizable vanilla tool and armor silhouettes, flat metal faces, selective chunky bright highlights from top left, dark clean pixel outlines and ordinary brown wooden handles. Neutral grayscale metal in six flat grey shades, brown handles. Each object fully fits its own cell with one logical pixel of transparent margin. Chestplate has broad shoulders and short body like vanilla iron chestplate item. Helmet has the simple vanilla rectangular hood shape. NOT smooth illustration, NOT 3D, NO antialiasing, NO gradients, NO tiny fake pixels, no gems or glowing fantasy details, no labels. Actual export target is 64 by 32 pixels.
export_notes: Rows 1–3 of metal-atlas supply ingots, samples and blocks. The complete equipment-atlas supplies all 15 equipment inventory sprites. The fourth metal-atlas row is retained as unused original source art. Export uses nearest-neighbor sampling, binary alpha, a six-tone per-material palette, and preserves brown wooden handles. Source atlases are build-time art inputs, not runtime resources. Armour worn on entities references Minecraft's native iron equipment texture and UVs with the material colour.
